dedupe_keys.name: us dot complementary pnt and gps backup technologies demonstration 2020

description: This testbed demonstration evaluated technologies that could keep positioning, navigation and timing services going if GPS were disrupted. In March 2020 the US Department of Transportation's Volpe Center ran field demonstrations of eleven candidate technologies chosen through competitive acquisition, five at Joint Base Cape Cod in Massachusetts and six at NASA Langley Research Center in Virginia: two low-Earth-orbit satellite services (L-band and S-band), two fibre-optic timing systems based on White Rabbit Precision Time Protocol, a combination of map matching, inertial and ultra-wideband sensors, and terrestrial radio systems in low, medium and ultra-high frequency and Wi-Fi bands. The results, published in a report to Congress in 2021, concluded that no single technology replaces GPS and that the best route to resilient service is a diverse mix, which shaped the department's Complementary PNT Action Plan of 2023, updated in 2024. Coverage: two US test sites in 2020, with results framed for transportation and other critical sectors. Format and access: free report in the DOT ROSA P repository and action plans on transportation.gov. Caveats: short vendor-run demonstrations under test conditions; commercial readiness and costs were not fully assessed. Simulation uses: parameters for resilience studies of backup timing and positioning, capacity planning of complementary systems, and hazard scenarios of GPS jamming. Related records: the RTI and NIST study gives outage costs, Jammertest in Norway tests receivers under interference, and the UK PNT framework chose eLoran.
